title: Framework Config Schema
description: Schema for framework-config.json — IDPF framework project configuration. Validates both self-hosted dev repos and PHM-deployed user projects via the optional selfHosted field.

$schema.description: JSON Schema reference (relative path to this schema file)

processFramework.description: Active process framework methodology. IDPF-Vibe was removed in #2530 when its directory was retired. IDPF-Structured and IDPF-LTS likewise have no directory; their removal was deliberately deferred there and is recorded as a decision, not an oversight.

domainSpecialist.description: Active domain specialist role (top-level — written by /change-domain-expert and PHM). Constrained to the framework-manifest.json domainSpecialists allowlist (#2503): an unconstrained string let path traversal and absolute paths reach the startup hook's path.join. Since #2533 the manifest holds objects and this enum derives from their `name` fields, so it now admits the eight announce-only entries (`loadable: false`) alongside the seventeen with files — selectable is a broader set than loadable, and this enum governs selection. 'Framework-Developer' is additionally permitted as the self-hosted maintainer role — no specialist file backs it, so the hook treats it as announce-only. It is deliberately NOT in framework-manifest.json, where it would break validate-helpers.js parity against constants.js and the e2e-verification count-vs-files-on-disk check. Enum/manifest parity is enforced by tests/scripts/framework/framework-config.test.js.

reviewSweep.description: How prior-art sweeping behaves in this project (#2514, remodelled #2564). Four modes, most to least sweeping: 'full' sweeps automatically at review time; 'recommend' never sweeps automatically but surfaces an advisory naming the command to run; 'flag-only' never sweeps automatically and shows no advisory; 'off' additionally refuses an explicit --prior-art, reporting the refusal and naming this setting. Only 'full' sweeps automatically. Absent means 'recommend', and both writers (Praxis Hub Manager at install/upgrade, and the review commands on first encounter) materialise the key, so the fallback governs only the window before the first write. Legacy booleans still validate and are migrated by normalizeReviewSweep: true becomes 'full', false becomes 'flag-only' — false has always meant 'no automated sweeps, but --prior-art still works', so mapping it to 'off' would silently remove a capability opted-out projects have. There is no second copy of this value anywhere, and no fallback lookup into .claude/metadata/, which is a read-only hub junction downstream. This is the only lever available between framework releases, since installed hub roots are frozen per version.

anyOf.description: Legacy pre-#2564 form. true migrates to 'full', false to 'flag-only'.

activeDomains.description: Active domain extensions for review criteria (lowercase domain IDs)

projectSkills.description: Skills installed in this project (sourced from .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md, sorted alphabetically). This is the installation contract: the full installed set. It is NOT what /context's 'Project' Skills section lists — that section shows only the model-invocable subset, so a skill whose SKILL.md frontmatter carries disable-model-invocation: true is absent there by design while remaining installed and loadable by the commands that read it. A shorter projectSkills list than /context, or vice versa, is expected and not a defect. See Reference/Project-Skills-Semantics.md.

suggestedSkills.description: Confirmed skill suggestions persisted by /create-prd for px-manager discovery

deploymentTarget.description: Deployment platform selected during /charter (null when self-hosted or no platform chosen)

installedDate.description: Date framework was installed (ISO date or YYYY-MM-DD)

frameworkPath.description: Absolute path to the framework root (or '.' for self-hosted)

selfHosted.description: Whether this project self-hosts the framework (true only for idpf-praxis-dev itself)

testCoverageAudit.description: Project-level override for the tdd-refactor-coverage-audit skill, read by its test-coverage-audit.js and merged over the bundled conventions. Deliberately loosely-typed: the authoritative shape is defined in that skill, at resources/test-coverage-conventions-schema.json, which ships from idpf-praxis-skills and declares JSON Schema 2020-12 while this file declares draft-07 — so a $ref cannot span the two, and restating the shape here is the cross-repo coupling that produced #2596. Shape validation is therefore deferred to the skill, which is admissible only because the failure is loud rather than silent: a block that does not match is reported as "framework-config.json -> testCoverageAudit failed schema validation", not ignored. This schema guarantees only that the key is permitted and is an object.

testCommand.description: The project's full-suite test command, invoked verbatim by /work Step 4f and by the once-per-sub-issue full-suite verification in Step 3. A command string rather than a runner name from an allowlist: the rule must work for `node --test`, `go test ./...`, `pytest -q` and `dotnet test` equally, and any enumeration would be a list of the ecosystems this framework happens to know about today. OPTIONAL, and absent is a valid steady state: Praxis Hub Manager does not seed this key (#2595 leaves that to px-manager), so most projects start without it. When it is absent /work reports that the sweep could not be run and proceeds unverified — it does NOT fall back to a substitute. A fallback correct for Node and silently wrong for Go, Rust and .NET would reintroduce the defect this key exists to fix, so the absence is made visible instead of being papered over.

crossSessionMessaging.description: Project-level governance of cross-session peer messaging (#2702). ABSENCE MEANS FULLY ENABLED, and that rule holds at every level: an omitted key inside the object is enabled too, so a config only ever records what was turned OFF and a group added by a future release is on by default in every existing project without a config edit. Read through .claude/scripts/shared/lib/cross-session-config.js resolveCrossSessionConfig() — no consumer re-derives these defaults inline, because a second copy of the absence rule is how the two drift. It lives here rather than in .claude/metadata/ because that directory is a read-only hub junction in PHM-deployed projects, so a deployed project could not otherwise disable a poller running inside it; framework-config.json is the only project-writable surface, the same reasoning that placed reviewSweep here (#2564). Written by /x-session-config. This governs EMISSION only: whether a dispatched message is accepted, held, declined or left to expire is the receiving session's permission-mode decision and is undetectable from the sender (#2674), so no setting here can promise delivery.

enabled.description: Master switch. False disables every other lever below, including discovery and the upstream monitor.

discovery.description: Governs peers-check.js and the startup 'Peers:' row. False IMPLIES all three groups off — announcing to peers that were never discovered is not meaningful — and the resolver reports that implication rather than silently zeroing them, because the user set one key and got four effects. False still emits a 'Peers:' row saying discovery is off by config: rule 03-startup.md already assigns 'no row' the meaning 'no peers found', and reusing it for 'not looked' would make a configured project indistinguishable from a lone one.

notices.description: Governs the dispatch-caveat and skip-reason lines printed once per announcement (#2672, #2674). False suppresses the printed notice only; dispatch itself is unchanged.

upstreamMonitor.description: Governs whether the background upstream-push poller arms (#2667). The monitor's scheduling values — intervals, backoff, push window — stay in .claude/metadata/upstream-monitor.json; only the whether-it-arms decision is a project decision. False makes the monitor report the reason once, not once per poll.

groups.description: Per-command event groups. Groups rather than per-event toggles because peer-announce.js guarantees every event 3 (push-started) is followed by exactly one terminal event (4 ci-terminal or 5 push-rejected). Per-event toggles would make 'push-started enabled, ci-terminal disabled' expressible in valid config, leaving a peer waiting forever for a message that will never arrive. Grouping makes that combination UNREPRESENTABLE, which is stronger than validating against it. The groups are also the emitting commands, so the setting a user reasons about is the setting that exists.

work.description: Events 1 work-started and 2 work-completed, emitted by /work Step 3 and Step 6 (#2662).

push.description: Events 3 push-started, 4 ci-terminal and 5 push-rejected, emitted by /done Step 2 and Step 3 (#2663). Governed as one unit — see the groups description.

review.description: Events 6 review-started and 7 review-resolved, emitted by /review-issue and /resolve-review (#2695).

verificationMode.description: How this project's TDD RED/GREEN gates are satisfied (#2556). `automated-tests` (the default when the key is ABSENT) keeps the strict gate: RED requires a test run executed against a runner that fails with the expected error. `host-process` is the carve-out for code that CANNOT BE EXECUTED OUTSIDE A LIVE HOST PROCESS — Unity, Unreal, Godot, embedded and firmware targets, and plugin or mod work. Under it RED is satisfied by the expected behaviour described in writing, and GREEN by verification in the actual runtime with the verification method and its captured output NAMED. The gate is not removed; it demands different evidence. The trigger is the impossibility of out-of-host execution, NOT the absence of tests: a project that could run automated tests but has not set them up declares `automated-tests` and remains subject to the strict gate. Keying on 'no tests exist' would turn a narrow carve-out into a universal opt-out. OPTIONAL, and absent is a valid steady state — every existing project is unchanged, and an unrecognised value on disk resolves to the strict default rather than the carve-out, so a typo can never become a silent gate bypass. Declared HERE rather than in the tdd-checklist.json this gate is loaded from, deliberately: that file belongs to the imported `tdd-process` skill, whose own schema is `additionalProperties: false` and which /fw-import-skills replaces wholesale, so any field added there is reverted at the next import. Mirroring this into the skill is a cross-repo change against idpf-praxis-skills, not something this repository can deliver.
